title: Pinsker-type bound via the KL integral
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and write $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the (real-valued) Radon–Nikodym density. Suppose the log-likelihood ratio $x \mapsto \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then
\[
   rac{1}{2}\left(\int_{\Omega} \left| rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) - 1ight|\,d
u(x)ight)^{2}
  \;\le\;
  \int_{\Omega} \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)\,d\mu(x),
\]
where the inner integral on the left is the $L^{1}(
u)$-distance of the density from the constant $1$.
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are probability measures on a measurable space Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
the log-likelihood ratio log(dμ/dν) is μ-integrable
